bib.title: When Not to Trust Language Models: Investigating Effectiveness of Parametric and Non-Parametric Memories
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 9802-9822

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; Table 3/4 qualitative example rows not read in detail.

question: When do LMs memorize factual knowledge, how much do scale and retrieval help, and can retrieval be used only when needed?
hypothesis: Factual knowledge frequently discussed on the web is easily memorized by LMs, while less discussed knowledge is not and needs retrieved non-parametric memory.
contributions: POPQA: 14k entity-centric questions over long-tail entities
Large-scale probing of 10 LMs showing memorization depends on subject popularity and relation type, and that scaling mostly helps popular facts
Adaptive Retrieval: retrieve only when subject popularity is below a per-relation threshold

method.summary: Probe ten LMs (GPT-Neo, OPT, GPT-3) closed-book on POPQA and EntityQuestions, add top-1 retrieved paragraph (BM25, Contriever) or generated context (GenRead), then gate retrieval by Wikipedia page-view popularity thresholds tuned per relation.

datasets.name: POPQA
datasets.size: 14k questions (14,267 in Fig 4; 14,282 in Appendix B), 16 relation types
datasets.split: 75% / 25% random split repeated 100 times for threshold selection and evaluation
datasets.source: Wikidata triples verbalised with manual templates; popularity = Wikipedia monthly page views
datasets.preprocessing: Triples sampled with weight to popularity: keep iff f > exp(8R-6), R~U(0,1), f = exact-match frequency of subject aliases in an 800 MB random sample of C4; cap 2000 triples per relation

datasets.name: EntityQuestions
datasets.size: 82% of questions (unique subject entity match to Wikidata); 24 relation types in Fig 18

datasets.name: NQ-open
datasets.preprocessing: Used only for the popularity distribution in Fig 3 (TagMe, score threshold 0.22)

models.name: Contriever
models.architecture: dense retriever pretrained on unlabeled corpora, fine-tuned on MS MARCO

inference.samples: one pass per question; no seeds stated; thresholds averaged over 100 random 75/25 splits
inference.prompting: Template 'Q: <question> A:'; zero-shot for GPT-3 (cost), 15-shot for GPT-Neo/OPT; POPQA shots: one random QA pair from each of the 15 other relations; EntityQuestions: simple random 15
inference.retrieval: Top-1 Wikipedia paragraph (Dec 2018 dump), concatenated with question; BM25 or Contriever; GenRead prompts LM to generate a context document

parameters.popularity_threshold: per relation type, brute-force search maximising adaptive accuracy on 75% of POPQA
parameters.adaptive_accuracy: retrieval-augmented prediction below threshold, parametric prediction above

other.quantisation: int8 for OPT 13B and GPT-Neo 20B; single V100 32GB for models >2B

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: correct if any substring of the prediction exact-matches any gold answer

metrics.name: recall@1
metrics.definition: whether a gold answer is in the top-1 retrieved document

metrics.name: correlation
metrics.definition: correlation between log-popularity bin centre and bin accuracy, uniform bins

eval.protocol: Wilson 95% CIs on binned accuracy; bins under 40 (Fig 8) or 5 (Figs 20-21) samples dropped; no significance tests

results.claim: The 4,000 least popular POPQA questions stay near 16-19% accuracy from GPT-j 6B to GPT-3 davinci-003, so scaling does not fix the long tail.
results.setup: POPQA (14k questions, 16 relations), closed-book, Q:/A: template, exact-match-substring accuracy; 4,000 least popular questions; GPT-3 zero-shot, others 15-shot
results.quote: for the 4,000 least popular questions in POPQA, GPT-j 6B has 16% accuracy and GPT-3 davinci-003 has 19% accuracy
results.note: Section 4.2 gives GPT-Neo 6B 15%, 20B 16%, davinci-003 19% for the same slice.

results.claim: Contriever-augmented GPT-Neo 2.7B beats vanilla GPT-3 davinci-003 on the 4,000 least popular questions.
results.setup: POPQA, top-1 Wikipedia paragraph (Dec 2018 dump) from Contriever, 15-shot GPT-Neo vs zero-shot davinci-003
results.quote: a neural dense retriever (Izacard et al., 2022a)-augmented GPT-neo 2.7B outperforms GPT-3 davinci-003 on the 4,000 least popular questions

results.claim: Retrieval gives GPT-3 davinci-003 a 7% accuracy gain even though it is the largest model.
results.setup: POPQA, top-1 Contriever paragraph, zero-shot davinci-003
results.quote: Contriever gives 7% accuracy gains on top of GPT-3 davinci-003

results.claim: For 10% of questions retrieval flips a correct GPT-3 answer to wrong, and Contriever recall@1 there is 0.14 against 0.42 overall.
results.setup: POPQA, GPT-3 davinci-003 with vs without Contriever top-1 paragraph; 10% of questions in the 'LM succeeded, retrieval failed' cell
results.quote: recall@1 is significantly lower than the overall recall@1 (0.14 vs 0.42 overall)

results.claim: For 17% of questions retrieval rescues a wrong GPT-3 answer, with recall@1 of 0.88.
results.quote: the 17% of questions for which retrieval causes the LM to correctly answer a question it would otherwise have failed to answer, the recall@1 is 0.88
results.note: Quote text is in the same sentence as 'for' after line break; number 0.88 also in Table 1.

limits: Relies on two synthetic, template-based entity datasets; transfer to naturally occurring knowledge not established (Limitations).
Adaptive Retrieval effectiveness depends on QA pipeline details; popularity is time-dependent and page views are one proxy.
Only entity-centric factual knowledge; commonsense is an open question.
Only top-1 retrieved paragraph, Dec 2018 Wikipedia, models up to ~175B (2022-era); GenRead and BM25 run on fewer models for EntityQuestions due to compute.
Gate needs subject entity and relation type linked from the question; the popularity threshold is tuned per relation on labelled data.
No decoding settings stated; no seeds.

terms.definition: decides when to retrieve passages only based on input query information and augments the input with retrieved non-parametric memories only when necessary

figures.why: Crossover curve that motivates a popularity gate.
